analysis.title: Four Takeaways for the Midterm Elections
key_insights: Morgan Stanley expects little legislative policy variance from the November 2026 midterms. The bar for macro impact is high, and the main effects are sector-specific, in Treasury supply and in the dollar.

Executive-led policy (tariffs, trade, deregulation, immigration, export controls) stays with the White House and is unchanged in every outcome. Policy uncertainty since January 2025 has come from executive action, not legislation.

Fiscal policy is the most election-sensitive variable, but the range is narrow. It centers on the timing of SNAP and Medicaid cuts, defense spending, and the severity of shutdown and debt-limit standoffs.

Three scenarios are framed: a Republican hold, a cohesive ('robust') Democratic majority that can use must-pass bills as leverage, and a fragile Democratic majority that is divided and mostly gridlocked.

Prediction markets price chamber control at 7% for a Republican sweep, 61% for a Democratic sweep and 31% for a split with a Democratic House and Republican Senate. The note says these odds do not capture caucus cohesion.
The midterms are not read as a signal for 2028. Midterms typically do not produce outsized over- or under-performance in the following 3-6 months, and the president keeps veto power for two years.

Midterm issues do not reliably carry into presidential years. Across six midterm-to-presidential pairs since 1994, the top-ranked issue changed in five. The decisive issue was visible at the prior midterm in only two.

Four debates are flagged as 2028 signals: social security and fiscal policy (Senate races in ME, MI, TX, NH), individual taxes (CA billionaire wealth tax against NC and OK tax-relief measures), data center restrictions, and healthcare (single payer versus a public option).

AI sentiment is assessed on two vectors. Data center opposition is a clear midterm catalyst, while AI safety and regulation is not. Sentiment is most constructive under a Republican sweep, neutral under divided government and weakest under a Democratic sweep.

Base case for AI capex is a conditional buildout. Binding levers over data centers (interconnection, large-load rates, siting, permitting, tax abatements) sit with states, utility commissions and governors, so those races matter more than Senate races.
Most candidates have converged on data center restrictions. The remaining argument is a pause versus conditions, and tax breaks are the consensus target regardless of who wins.

A federal data center ban is unlikely near term because of the national-security framing, the US-China AI race and likely presidential veto. The midterms could lay groundwork for federal action after 2028.

Comprehensive AI regulation is unlikely near term without a high-salience incident, and any response to such an incident should be bipartisan. Near-term actions stay voluntary, and executive action leads on model and tech restrictions.

Equities: seasonality turns supportive from October. A Democratic outperformance could cause a near-term move lower, which Morgan Stanley thinks would not be sustained. The type of majority matters more than which party wins.

Rates: coupon auction sizes should rise in every outcome, so only deficits larger than investors expect should move the curve. A unified Republican government keeps a party-line reconciliation bill available and is the main upside risk to Treasury supply. Extra issuance would land in the 2-7 year sector, cheapening the belly and flattening 5s30s.

A cohesive Democratic majority closes the reconciliation route. Delaying SNAP and Medicaid cuts adds roughly $130 billion if both slip a year, which is small against a deficit near $2 trillion. Focus shifts to the December funding deadline and the 2027 debt limit.
A fragile Democratic majority brings the least supply pressure and lower rate volatility, but also the least dollar support from yields and the clearest growth downside from shutdown risk.

FX: unified Republican control gives the most USD upside, with short EUR/USD and EUR/AUD. A cohesive Democratic majority gives little yield direction, with value in long-dated USD optionality in CNY, CAD and MXN. A fragile majority favors long JPY and CHF against high-beta currencies.

EM sovereign credit: slight positive for Trump-aligned LatAm sovereigns (Argentina, Venezuela, Ecuador, El Salvador, Colombia) under a Republican win. Slight negative if Democrats win, for those relying on unorthodox support such as the Argentina swap line and the Venezuela oil deal. Practical impact is limited because these sit outside appropriations.

Sector map: a Republican win favors defense, financials, nuclear energy and data center REITs, with consumer staples, retail and restaurants slightly negative. A Democratic sweep favors consumer staples and healthcare services or managed care, with renewables slightly positive. Divided government favors data center REITs and managed care.
Equity markets show diminishing sensitivity to presidential social-media headlines on tariffs and the US-Iran conflict. Treasuries sold off more often after posts with a clear macro read-across.

If AI capex falls short, the hit to growth is meaningful, with 0.60 percentage points of 2027 real GDP growth tied to AI capex. Owners of compute (hyperscalers) gain scarcity value and AI adopters lose. Credit spreads could tighten as issuance falls.

AI labor disruption is modest but visible. Unemployment in highly AI-exposed occupations runs about 0.5 percentage points above the cyclical-adjusted level, up from 0.3 in December 2025, and the signal is strongest for workers aged 22-27.

Munis: California's billionaire wealth tax, Washington's millionaire tax repeal vote and Florida's property tax cut are the key ballot measures. A cohesive Democratic majority could defer SNAP and Medicaid cuts, which matter for state finances.
Biopharma: large caps framed the policy backdrop as fairly neutral. 340B and PBM reform have bipartisan momentum, and Medicare for All is seen as a tail risk rather than a 2027-28 path.
Morgan Stanley's Kalshi work finds Kalshi pricing useful for fed funds and CPI, where accuracy beats common indicators. It has not yet extended the analysis to election markets.

sector_views.rationale: Higher defense spending growth is more likely under unified Republican control. Spending is still negotiated in split-government outcomes.
Continued deregulation under a Republican win supports growth, capital deployment and capital markets activity. Oversight under divided government slows but does not derail it.
Fossil and nuclear expansion is favored under a Republican win. A cohesive Democratic sweep is more supportive of renewables.

sector_views.sector: Consumer staples, hardlines, broadlines and food retail
sector_views.rationale: SNAP cuts weigh on low-income demand if implemented as legislated. Delays under a cohesive Democratic majority limit the downside.
Gridlock or a Democratic sweep reduces the prospect of major Medicaid, Medicare Advantage and ACA changes. That gives earnings visibility for managed care.
Republican control risks non-renewal of refundable tax credits that support lower-income demand. Democratic transfer support helps low-end demand.
MFN codification is unlikely in either Democratic outcome. 340B and PBM reform are the focus and have bipartisan support.
Divided government is the most favorable for pricing power. A Republican sweep eases permitting and energy access.

macro_indicators.indicator: US federal deficit as share of GDP
macro_indicators.reading: around 6% in the next two years
macro_indicators.interpretation: A Republican win adds about 0.2pp of upside risk in 2027 from defense spending. A cohesive Democratic sweep adds about 0.2pp through delayed SNAP and Medicaid cuts.
A slower AI buildout would cut growth and could dampen wealth-effect consumption.

macro_indicators.indicator: Cohesive Democratic majority effect on GDP
macro_indicators.reading: upside of a couple tenths of a percentage point
macro_indicators.interpretation: Scaled-back SNAP and Medicaid cuts would lift personal consumption.

macro_indicators.indicator: Treasury financing shortfall at current auction sizes
macro_indicators.interpretation: Larger coupon auctions arrive in every outcome, so only deficits above investor expectations should move the curve.

macro_indicators.indicator: Treasury bill share of marketable debt
macro_indicators.interpretation: The debt limit binds during 2027, and bills maturing around the x-date have cheapened most consistently.

macro_indicators.reading: roughly +22% in the 12 months after the election
macro_indicators.interpretation: Seasonality turns supportive from October, though slowing earnings growth suggests more modest gains than in recent years.

macro_indicators.reading: reserves exhaust in late 2032, revenue then covers roughly 78% of scheduled benefits
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports a 2028 election focus on Social Security reform.

crypto_views: Powered shell providers with bitcoin-mining roots (CIFR, WULF, HUT, RIOT, GLXY) are named as beneficiaries if data center backlash slows capex or if behind-the-meter power is favored.
Morgan Stanley rates MARA Underweight, CIFR, HUT, RIOT and WULF Overweight, and APLD Equal-weight in the coverage tables.
Crypto regulation is listed among policy areas with potential for compromise, and is cited as an example where statute is the only route.

trade_ideas.description: Own long-dated USD optionality in CNY, CAD and MXN, the pairs most exposed to targeted trade action, in a Democratic sweep scenario
trade_ideas.rationale: If blocked in Congress, the White House may lean harder on tariffs and sanctions, which may be selectively USD supportive when narrowly targeted.

trade_ideas.description: Short EUR/USD and short EUR/AUD in a unified Republican control scenario
trade_ideas.rationale: Larger spending lifts 2-7 year US yields and nominal growth, boosting the USD and high-beta currencies against low yielders.
trade_ideas.risk: Treasury and Japan's Ministry of Finance intervention could limit USD/JPY gains.

trade_ideas.description: Long JPY and CHF versus high-beta currencies (AUD, NOK, GBP) in a fragile Democratic majority scenario, rather than a dollar view
trade_ideas.rationale: Yields offer the least dollar support, while repeated funding fights and shutdown risk point to growth downside and subdued risk demand.

trade_ideas.description: In a Republican win, expect the Treasury belly to cheapen and the 5s30s curve to flatten
trade_ideas.rationale: A party-line reconciliation bill adds issuance in the 2-7 year sector, while AI-related corporate supply sets the marginal price of duration at the long end.
trade_ideas.risk: Only deficits larger than investors expect should move the curve.

risk_factors: A Democratic outperformance could cause a near-term equity move lower on regime uncertainty and data center pushback.
A reconciliation bill under unified Republican control could add to Treasury borrowing needs beyond what investors expect.
Shutdown and debt-limit standoffs in a fragile Democratic majority, with the 2027 debt limit and the December funding deadline as flashpoints.
A White House leaning harder on tariffs and sanctions if blocked in Congress.
A high-salience AI incident could trigger legislation, and a shift in public opposition toward safety concerns could remove the need for one.
Frontier model release slowdowns from government intervention, or loss of US lab market share to Chinese open-weight models, could hurt data center capex sentiment.
State and local anti-data-center challengers winning could prolong moratoriums and raise federal restrictions as a 2029 tail risk.
Capex slowdown would hit AI adopters and weigh on growth, with 0.60pp of 2027 GDP growth tied to AI capex.
Local ballot measures (CA wealth tax, WA millionaire tax repeal, FL property tax cut) carry capital flight and municipal credit risks.
Medicare for All reviving as a 2028 theme if single-payer candidates lead a large Democratic margin.
charts_described: Exhibit 10 shows 72% of likely voters say candidates' AI positions are very or somewhat important to their vote (34% very, 38% somewhat).
Exhibit 26 shows AI-exposure unemployment tracker: the cyclical-adjustment residual for high-exposure occupations is 0.5pp in the latest reading.
Exhibit 27 compares top midterm and presidential issues across six pairs from 1994-96 to 2022-24, with overlap of 1 to 3 of the top issues.
vol_and_positioning: The note expects narrower legislative variance, and so lower rate volatility, under a fragile Democratic majority.
Morgan Stanley expects uncertainty from a change in control to be a headwind to index-level prices under a cohesive Democratic sweep, similar to 2022 midterm volatility.
Defensive sectors have typically outperformed in the months before midterms. Growth, cyclicals and small caps have typically outperformed after the election.
geopolitical: US-China tech divergence and sovereign AI remain under presidential control, with executive tools (OFAC, FCC, import restrictions, Entity List, IEEPA) leading.

The Argentina swap line runs through the Treasury Exchange Stabilization Fund and the Venezuela oil deal rests on OFAC licensing, so both sit outside appropriations. A Democratic chamber could add oversight noise with limited near-term impact.
The US-Iran conflict is cited as a source of headline risk to which equity markets show diminishing sensitivity.
Treasury and Japan's Ministry of Finance have said they will not hesitate to intervene again after the July 31 operation, which may cap USD/JPY gains.
The AI OVERWATCH Act and the MATCH Act could be attached to the NDAA to make chip and equipment export controls more durable.

tension_points.bull_case: A Democratic outperformance would lead markets to price a higher chance of a Democratic presidency in 2028 and question the durability of deregulation and the OBBBA.
tension_points.bear_case: Morgan Stanley calls that reaction misplaced. Midterms do not produce outsized 3-6 month performance and the president keeps veto power for two years.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Democratic outperformance that comes with winning anti-data-center state and local races could shift the 2029 federal tail risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Republican sweep and pro-incumbent state outcomes remove the 2028 expectation and raise the odds of federal support. Mitigation pledges support a conditional buildout.
tension_points.bear_case: Anti-data-center challengers winning, plus a Democratic sweep, could prolong moratoriums and raise federal restriction risk in 2029.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sea change of anti-data-center challengers winning governor, utility commission and legislature races in TX, OH, PA, GA, NV, WI, MI, LA, MN or AZ.

tension_points.bull_case: A cohesive Democratic majority or gridlock removes reconciliation-driven supply and lowers rate volatility.
tension_points.bear_case: Unified Republican control keeps a reconciliation bill available, with defense and tax extensions adding to borrowing and cheapening the belly.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deficits larger than investors currently expect, which are the only thing the note says should move the curve.
